7 and the collected The Sermons of Maister Henrie
Smith (London, 1592), STC 22718.

Smith's collected sermons went through 21 editions between 1592 and 1675, see
Ian Green, Print and Protestantism in Early Modern England (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2000), 657.

The printing
history of the Nebuchadnezzar sermons and the collected sermons is notoriously complex. While the collected
sermons warn of earlier imprints in circulation made from "an unperfect Copie," the Short Title Catalogue (vol. 2, 339)
notes that the composition of the collection was in flux until c. 1600. Consequently, I cite the 1604 quarto volume
printed by Felix Kyngston for Thomas Man, Henry Smith, The Sermons of Master Henrie Smith (London, 1604), STC 22725.

4 Biblical references throughout are to the 1560 Geneva Bible: The bible and holy scriptures conteyned in the olde and newe
testament (1560), STC 2093. Note that the Geneva Bible followed the Vulgate in attributing Dan. 3:31-33 to the end of
Daniel 3. However, these three verses were shifted to Dan. 4:1-3 as an epistolary introduction to Nebuchadnezzar's fall
in the Coverdale (1535), Great (1539), Bishops' (1568) and King James (1611) Bibles. I have followed the verse number-
ing as it appears in the Geneva Version.
